author: Yamamoto-Imoto, Hara, et al.

steps.title: Passage and plate hRPE1 cells
steps.instruction: Passage proliferative human retinal pigment epithelial (hRPE1) cells using Trypsin‑EDTA, then coat 35 mm culture dishes (Thermo Fisher 150460) with 2 mL Cellmatrix Type I‑C (Fujifilm Wako, 631‑00771, diluted 1:10 in ddH₂O); incubate 10 min at room temperature (20‑22 °C), wash twice with 2 mL PBS, and plate cells: (a) for senescence‑associated β‑galactosidase (SA‑β‑gal) staining on micro cover glasses (0.16–0.19 mm thickness) placed in the coated dish at 0.5 × 10⁵ cells per dish, and (b) for SDS‑PAGE/Western blot in 6‑well plates (Thermo Fisher 140675) at 0.5–1.0 × 10⁵ cells per well. Incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ in a humidified chamber.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Cellmatrix Type I‑C coating solution (1:10 dilution).
Add 2 mL coating solution to each 35 mm dish, incubate 10 min RT.
Wash dishes twice with 2 mL PBS.
Place micro cover glass in coated dish and plate 0.5 × 10⁵ cells for SA‑β‑gal.
Plate 0.5–1.0 × 10⁵ cells per well in 6‑well plates for Western blot.
Incubate cells 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Incubate cells post‑doxorubicin
steps.instruction: Allow cells to recover for 10 days after doxorubicin treatment before evaluating senescent state.

steps.title: Prepare samples for SA‑β‑gal staining
steps.instruction: Wash each dish with 2 mL PBS, add 2 mL 1× Fixation Buffer and incubate 7 min at room temperature, then wash three times with 2 mL PBS; samples may be stored in PBS at 4 °C for up to one week.

substeps.instruction: Wash dish with 2 mL PBS and discard.
Add 2 mL 1× Fixation Buffer; incubate 7 min RT.
Wash dish three times with 2 mL PBS each.
Store in PBS at 4 °C (optional, up to 1 week).

steps.title: Prepare lysates for Western blot
steps.instruction: Wash each well twice with 2 mL cold PBS, add 25 µL lysis buffer (adjust 25–100 µL based on cell number), scrape on ice, pipette 7 times, transfer to a microcentrifuge tube, centrifuge 20,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C, collect supernatant, determine protein concentration with Pierce BCA Protein Assay Kit (Thermo Fisher, 23225), normalize all samples with lysis buffer, add 5× SDS‑sample buffer, heat 95 °C for 7 min, then cool 5 min at room temperature; supernatants can be stored ≤‑80 °C and heated samples ≤‑20 °C until use.

substeps.instruction: Wash well twice with 2 mL cold PBS; discard.
Add 25 µL lysis buffer (25–100 µL as needed).
Scrape cells on ice and pipette 7 times to lyse.
Transfer lysate to microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge 20,000 × g, 15 min, 4 °C.
Collect supernatant.
Measure protein concentration with Pierce BCA kit (catalog 23225).
Adjust all samples to equal protein concentration using lysis buffer.
Add 5× SDS‑sample buffer, mix well.
Heat at 95 °C for 7 min, then cool 5 min at RT.
Store supernatant ≤‑80 °C; store heated samples ≤‑20 °C.

steps.title: Stain cells for SA‑β‑gal activity
steps.instruction: Transfer the fixed cover glass from step 3 to a 24‑well plate containing PBS, remove PBS, add 1 mL staining mixture with X‑gal solution (Sigma, CS00030), seal with Parafilm, incubate 37 °C for 16–20 h without CO₂, wash three times with 1 mL PBS, cover with VECTASHIELD mounting medium with DAPI (H‑1200), image at 100× magnification (BX53 Olympus) using DIC and DAPI channels, count at least 200 DAPI‑positive cells, and calculate the percentage of SA‑β‑gal‑positive cells.

substeps.instruction: Place fixed cover glass into a 24‑well plate filled with PBS.
Remove PBS.
Add 1 mL staining mixture containing X‑gal (Sigma CS00030).
Seal plate with Parafilm.
Incubate 37 °C for 16–20 h without CO₂.
Wash cells three times with 1 mL PBS.
Add VECTASHIELD mounting medium with DAPI (H‑1200).
Image cells at 100× (BX53 Olympus) using DIC and DAPI.
Count ≥200 DAPI‑positive cells and compute % SA‑β‑gal‑positive.

steps.title: Optional alternative senescence assay
steps.instruction: Use the Cellular Senescence Plate Assay Kit – SPiDER‑βGal (Dojindo, SG05) together with the Cell Count Normalization Kit (Dojindo, C544) as alternatives for assessing SA‑β‑gal positivity.

description: CRITICAL: All materials for cell culture need to be sterile, and all sterile procedures handling cells need to be performed in a Class II biological safety cabinet under standard aseptic techniques.
